findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock. BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for its whole duration, and writes to the map happen concurrently from watch events and from Search via getOrCreateIndex. The PR also adds a TotalDocs call to the init log line, which runs after the watch goroutine has started. Concurrent map iteration and map write is a fatal runtime error in Go. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body: The whole-function lock is gone, and getOrCreateIndex has no per-key guard. Two callers that both miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource (for example a search request and a watch event, or two parallel searches) will now both build the index. For file-backed indexes the second bleve.New on the same directory fails or conflicts. For memory indexes the last writer silently replaces the cached index, and the replaced one is leaked, never closed. The finer-grained locking should also check the cache again under the lock, or use a per-key singleflight, rather than only locking around the map write.

findings.title: Heavy, blocking init in the constructor makes startup fail or hang
findings.body: NewResourceServer now runs lifecycle Init, the full search index build for every namespace, and the watcher synchronously. Any failure, such as a transient DB error while building one index, now makes the constructor return an error and aborts server creation. Previously this failed only the first request. Construction time grows with data size, which can stall Grafana startup, and a wire-injected dependency now does I/O at construction. The PR itself asks whether anything depends on lazy init, and the postgres test being skipped suggests something does. Also, Init is now never re-invoked, so calls after a failed Stop no longer return the initErr and instead proceed against a stopped server.

findings.title: Test skipped for postgres to hide a failure caused by this change
findings.body: The test is skipped for postgres in Drone with only a TODO, apparently because eager initialization breaks it there. This removes coverage for the new startup path and masks a likely real regression instead of fixing it. At minimum it needs a tracking issue.

findings.title: Trace context still discarded in several places despite the PR claiming a fix
findings.body: bleveBackend.BuildIndex still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, so the span context is not propagated. The same is true in sql/backend.go for WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator, which also discard the returned ctx. Only GetResourceStats was fixed, so the traces stay fragmented.

findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
findings.body: The errgroup goroutines all assign to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increment `totalBatchesIndexed++` without synchronization. Init now runs eagerly with many workers over many namespaces, so the race is exercised at startup. The reported count and returned error can be wrong, and the race detector will flag it. Use a local err and an atomic counter.
